newsitem.title: UK: Physical cocoa mart quiet, some light origin sales.
newsitem.headline: Physical cocoa mart quiet, some light origin sales.

text.p: The physical cocoa market remained quiet this week, with the main feature coming from origins.

Ivory Coast and Ghana were the main sellers in the futures market, helping to cap any rally, traders said. They said Ghana was selling to hedge the current and new crop while the Ivory Coast, already well sold for the current crop, concentrated on the new crop.
Cocoa futures have inched higher this week, with July edging up to the highest level since April 29.

On the physical market, Ivory Coast differentials for nearby June/July were seen about 30 to 40 under terminal for sellers' prices. Forwards were seen about 25 under for the new crop. Both were about steady from last week.

One physicals trader said Ivory Coast was in the market daily, taking advantage of prices near 900 to 950 francs in January/March and April/May registrations. He said those prices have not been seen for a few years.
But traders still expected prices to stay steady, locked in a range until a fundamental shift in the market surfaces.
July cocoa futures were still seen trapped in a wide range between 1,060 stg per tonne and about 990 for the next couple of months or until more about the Ivory Coast midcrop is known.

On the demand said, sterling's gains earlier this week dampened enthusiasm in the physicals market though the UK unit has come off a bit so far on Thursday. With sterling near current levels, Europeans have had a difficult time being competitive.
Traders said demand could pick up if cocoa futures prices dropped 30 stg or if the British currency gave up the equivalent.
